title.value: Stroke Lesion Segmentation in FLAIR MRI Datasets Using Customized Markov Random Fields
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the specific focus of the research which involves using Customized Markov Random Fields for stroke lesion segmentation in FLAIR MRI datasets.
title.quote: Subbanna NK, Rajashekar D, Cheng B, Thomalla G, Fiehler J, Arbel T and Forkert ND (2019) Stroke Lesion Segmentation in FLAIR MRI Datasets Using Customized Markov Random Fields. Front. Neurol. 10:541. doi: 10.3389/fneur.2019.00541

analysis.description: The paper presents a novel method for segmenting stroke lesions from FLAIR MRI datasets using a combination of Bayesian techniques and Markov Random Fields. This method leverages Gabor textures to improve the segmentation accuracy compared to manual segmentations and is compared against other state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its efficacy.

type.justification: The study presents a novel method for stroke lesion segmentation and quantitatively evaluates its performance against other state-of-the-art methods. It uses real-world data and empirical testing to validate its proposed method.
type.quote: The proposed method was developed and evaluated based on 151 multi-center datasets from three different databases using a leave-one-patient-out validation approach.

name.justification: The paper focuses on stroke lesion segmentation using MRI datasets, which is a common application within the field of Medical Imaging.
name.quote: The aim of this work was to develop and evaluate a novel method to segment sub-acute ischemic stroke lesions from fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets.

name.justification: The paper involves the analysis of MRI datasets to segment stroke lesions, thus fitting under the MRI Analysis sub-research field.
name.quote: The aim of this work was to develop and evaluate a novel method to segment sub-acute ischemic stroke lesions from fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets.

name.justification: The paper compares its proposed method with methods based on Convolutional Neural Networks, indicating their use.
name.quote: Furthermore, the results obtained by the proposed technique are superior compared to the results obtained by two methods based on convolutional neural networks and three phase level-sets.

is_contributed.justification: Convolutional Neural Networks are referenced as baseline methods for comparison, not a novel contribution in the paper.
is_contributed.quote: Furthermore, the results obtained by the proposed technique are superior compared to the results obtained by two methods based on convolutional neural networks and three phase level-sets.

is_executed.justification: The comparison is based on results reported from previous studies, not on the execution of these models within the paper.
is_executed.quote: The first technique (31) is a method based on convolutional neural networks... The comparison techniques were re-implemented based on the code available from the authors.

is_compared.justification: The performance of the proposed method is compared with CNN based methods, indicating numerical comparison.
is_compared.quote: Furthermore, the results obtained by the proposed technique are superior compared to the results obtained by two methods based on convolutional neural networks and three phase level-sets.

referenced_paper_title.quote: Kamnitsas K, Chen L, Ledig C, Rueckert D, Glocker B. Multi-Scale 3D convolutional neural networks for lesion segmentation in brain MRI.

name.justification: I-KNOW is one of the three databases used for developing and evaluating the proposed lesion segmentation method.
name.quote: The second database consists of 108 FLAIR datasets acquired within a prospective European multi-center stroke imaging study (I-KNOW) from a total of five contributing centers.
